rules.rationale: Source ESOL: long SMILES reduced solubility (-11.46); hydration affinity often inversely related to molecular size.
Hydrogen-bond donors (heteroatoms) donate water hydrogen bonds, raising hydration affinity.
Ring-rich molecules pack poorly in water, lowering hydration affinity; source ring_bin transferred strongly (w=0.76).
Halogen substitution weakens hydrogen bonding, reducing hydration affinity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL solubility effects: small heterocyclics score highest, large ring-rich halogenated candidates lowest. Fails if hydration affinity tracks polar surface area rather than size.

rules.rationale: Small heterocycles maximize polar surface area per atom, the dominant hydration driver.
Large halogenated solutes have low polar surface area and poor water packing.
Aromatic surfaces hydrate poorly, so aromaticity should lower hydration affinity.
Ring-free acyclic scaffolds pack well in water, raising hydration affinity.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis: hydration affinity tracks polar surface area, not size. Fails if the source smiles_length effect (+6.89/-6.61/-11.46) carries across.

state.lesson: Across two development seeds, both skills reached the same final best score (95.4), so the seed-level differences in AUC and final best are unreliable. The source-grounded skill's mean AUC (81.2) was higher than the counter-hypothesis (69.4), so the safer choice is to keep the size-and-HBond transfer and deploy it.
state.revision_summary: Kept the source-grounded skill intact and deployed it, since its mean performance was slightly better and the seed-level differences are too small to draw causal conclusions. The counter-hypothesis remains unchanged as a polar-surface-area alternative.
